source.version: abstract only (Crossref JATS abstract of the version of record, Architecture 6(3):133, published 2026-08-10; same text in Semantic Scholar). The MDPI HTML and PDF pages returned HTTP 403, so no full text was read.
source.title_on_document: Generative AI and the Reordering of Design Creativity in Architectural Education: Evidence from Undergraduate Students

paper_design_summary: In one first-year architecture studio, 45 students made a handmade bus-stop design and then reworked it with AI visualisation tools. Experts rated the pre-AI and post-AI designs on the same nine-dimension Consensual Assessment Technique rubric, and the authors linked the ratings to text-mined prompt logs. There is no comparison group and no random assignment: the authors call it an observational within-student design.

studies.label: First-year studio, handmade versus AI-refined bus-stop design

assignment.what_was_assigned: Nothing was assigned at random. Every student made a handmade design first and then reworked it with AI tools (fixed before-after order, no control group).
assignment.quote: As results are based on a single first-year cohort, institution, design brief, and an observational within-student design, the findings are limited to exploratory evidence

eligibility.reason: The abstract explicitly describes an observational within-student design, not random assignment (Crossref JATS abstract, final limitation sentence). It reports a cohort of 45 students who developed and then reworked their designs; this is below 50 people even though the final analyzed count and exclusions are not explicitly reported, so n_analyzed is null (methods sentence beginning "In a first-year studio"). Expert CAT ratings of the pre-AI and post-AI designs satisfy the output-scoring criterion (methods sentence beginning "Pre-AI and post-AI designs"). The non-randomized within-student comparison is observational context under the codebook. Source: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.3390/architecture6030133. The publisher HTML and PDF returned HTTP 403; no full text or appendices were read.

one_line_finding: In a reported cohort of 45 first-year architecture students, expert-rated total creativity of bus-stop designs rose from 3.38 before to 3.71 after AI refinement (Wilcoxon p = 0.022, dz = 0.38), with gains in appropriateness dimensions and no change in novelty, in an observational within-student design; the final analyzed count is not explicitly stated (Crossref JATS abstract, methods, results, and final limitation sentence).
